citation: La Bella et al. (2024), Concurrent Model-Based Approach for CubeSat Mission Design
title: Concurrent Model-Based Approach for CubeSat Mission Design
venue_type: conference, 75th International Astronautical Congress (IAC), Milan, Italy, 14-18 October 2024
modeling_scope: Concurrent model-based preliminary design approach for micro/nanosatellite and CubeSat missions, combining concurrent engineering with MBSE-supported digital tools. Scope covers mission design and analysis, ConOps, architecture, subsystem sizing, budgets, risk and cost, component selection, central data exchange, and general early verification. EPS is included as one S3D spreadsheet and as multiple CUTE-DB power technology categories, but EPS behavior modeling is not the paper's main focus.
mbse_language_method_tool: Concurrent Model-Based approach combining Concurrent Engineering and MBSE; S3D Tool implemented as Microsoft Excel calculation sheets plus Central Data Exchange System; CUTE-DB Excel-based CubeSat Technologies Database; supporting tools include STK, SolidWorks, Jira/Miro, Valispace, and PowerPoint. No SysML language is reported.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite missions; demonstrated on BOSS, a 12U CubeSat mission to Bennu, plus Geo-Profundo 6U LEO CubeSat and cislunar CubeSat inspector case studies.
task_domain: Preliminary phase 0/A CubeSat mission and system design for space exploration and observation, including BOSS asteroid in-situ observation/mapping, Geo-Profundo urban-growth monitoring and deep-space technology demonstration, and cislunar inspection feasibility.
interface: Central Data Exchange System links discipline spreadsheets for automated/manual data exchange across mission, system, subsystem, and component levels; all team members can access it, with check alerts for common inputs. Concurrent design sessions use discipline roles, shared presentations, and CUTE-DB for component selection.
feedback: Iterative design refinement and near-real-time concurrent teamwork are central: subsystem analyses feed the central repository, consistency checks flag shared-input issues, and each session ends with review of results and next-step definition. No closed-loop EPS simulation feedback is reported.
control_autonomy_split: BOSS operations mention autonomous attitude and trajectory control and navigation map generation, but no detailed control allocation or human-autonomy split is reported.
network_latency_assumptions: BOSS is described as communicating with ground stations through the mothership as relay; no network latency assumptions are reported.
evaluation: The approach was implemented and tested in several CubeSat case studies, with BOSS described in detail through four concurrent design sessions. Effectiveness is assessed by comparing BOSS feasibility-study outputs against a traditional methodology using mass budget, Delta-V budget, cost assessment, and feasibility-analysis duration.
rq_relevance: RQ1 yes: the paper presents a general Concurrent Model-Based approach for CubeSat mission design with system-level models/tools and EPS sizing/database coverage. RQ2 partial: it claims model-based/concurrent outcomes for faster design, transparency, integration, consistency, error reduction, cost/time reduction, and risk reduction, but it does not attribute reliability or reproducibility outcomes specifically to EPS modeling. RQ3 partial: it links early model integration to earlier verification and mentions design/testing support, but does not provide explicit verification procedures, IVV/test models, or EPS-specific verification procedures.
claimed_outcomes: Faster, more flexible, and transparent design management compared with traditional methods, simplifying system design flow and early decision-making.
Early model integration is claimed to allow system compatibility assessment, reduce errors and potential conflicts, and start verification earlier than traditional methodologies.

The approach is claimed to reduce development time, improve efficiency, quality, and overall performance, and reduce cost and risk through simultaneous engineering, iterative design, communication, and risk management.
The Central Data Exchange System is claimed to enable faster validation of sizing, budgets, and design, reducing manual effort and minimizing errors.

In the BOSS comparison, the CE-MBSE feasibility study reports 22.59 kg mass versus 26.6 kg, 15M€ cost versus 22M€, and 1 month duration versus 3 months for the traditional methodology; the CE-MBSE Delta-V budget is 1.33 m/s versus 0.68 m/s.
Reliability and reproducibility outcomes are not explicitly reported as outcomes of EPS modeling.
verification_validation_linkage: General linkage only: CE/MBSE tools are said to improve design, development, and verification, and early model integration is said to let verification begin in advance. The paper does not describe an explicit V&V, IVV, test-procedure model, or EPS-specific verification procedure.
key_findings: The proposed methodology combines concurrent engineering with MBSE to support phase 0/A CubeSat design through simultaneous system modelling and iterative refinement.
The S3D Tool provides discipline spreadsheets for CubeSat subsystem sizing and budgets, including EPS, ADCS, communications, propulsion, thermal, payload, risk, and cost.
The Central Data Exchange System shares data across mission, system, subsystem, and component levels and checks common input consistency across disciplines.

CUTE-DB is an Excel-based database of commercially available CubeSat technologies, including power system integrated units, solar cells, solar arrays, PCDUs, and batteries, with specifications such as physical, functional, environmental, power, heritage, and price fields.
The BOSS case study used four concurrent design sessions from mission objectives and ConOps through subsystem sizing, COTS component selection, final budgets, cost, and risk mitigation.
The comparison with traditional methodology suggests reduced feasibility-analysis duration and lower estimated cost for CE-MBSE, but the authors note the comparison excludes post-study refinement.
limitations_gaps: The paper states that the S3D Tool needs improvement and optimisation.
The Optical Payload calculation sheet needs updating and integration into the central repository, and dedicated spreadsheets for other payload types are needed.
A dedicated C&DH calculation sheet must be created to standardize performance calculations and requirements tracking.

Alternative environments such as Comet and Matlab System Composer are under investigation for improved model-based design, architecture definition, and collaboration, including possible later-phase applicability.
The CUTE-DB database management approach is still under discussion, with MySQL and other database solutions being evaluated for scalability and reliability.
The comparison with traditional methodology reports that results only account for the four sessions and not post-study refinement.
No formal threats-to-validity section is provided.

quality.rationale: Published as a 2024 IAC conference paper. It includes a lessons learned and way forward section with tool and database improvement needs, but no formal limitations or validity-threat discussion.

evidence_quotes.quote: This paper presents a novel Concurrent Model-Based approach for CubeSat mission design

evidence_quotes.claim: Concurrent model-based method combines CE and MBSE for micro/nanosatellites
evidence_quotes.quote: The Concurrent Model-Based approach combines the principles of CE and MBSE to achieve a more efficient and effective system design process for micro and nanosatellite missions and services

evidence_quotes.claim: S3D tool subsystem and EPS scope
evidence_quotes.quote: It consists of a set of calculation sheets implemented in Microsoft Excel dedicated to the main disciplines of the preliminary design phase of a CubeSat project: Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS), Communication System (CommSys), Electrical Power System (EPS), Propulsion System, Thermal Control System (TCS), Optical Payload, Risk, and Cost.

evidence_quotes.claim: Central data exchange and consistency checking
evidence_quotes.quote: This repository is linked to the other spreadsheets and allows for both automated and manual data input. Its purpose is to ensure that up-to-date information and data are shared across different disciplines and levels (mission, system, subsystem, component) while verifying that all disciplines operate on the same assumptions.

The current version of the CUTE-DB is an Excel-based database, covering several CubeSat technologies such as Deployers, Structures, Command and Data Handling (C&DH) systems, EPS, ADCS, CommSys, Propulsion Systems, Navigation Systems, Optical Payloads, TCS, Docking Systems, Mechanisms, and Platforms.

by integrating the models early in the development process, the system compatibility can be assessed, reducing errors and minimising potential conflicts, and the verification process can begin in advance with respect to traditional methodologies.
the Concurrent Model-Based approach can significantly reduce the development time of complex systems, improve their efficiency, quality, and overall performance, as well as reduce cost and risk.

evidence_quotes.claim: Implementation and evaluation through case studies
evidence_quotes.quote: the Concurrent Model-Based approach and the related tools (both S3D Tool and CUTE-DB) have been implemented and tested in several case studies, including the Bennu Observer Small Satellites (BOSS) mission, the Geo-Profundo mission, and the Cislunar mission
the final mission will consist of this concept of operation involving a 12U CubeSat launched on Falcon Heavy inside a mothercraft towards Bennu.
Using the CE-MBSE methodology, the feasibility study was completed in one month, compared to the three months required when using the traditional approach.
However, the shown results only take into account the 4 sessions results and not the post-study refinement.

evidence_quotes.claim: Explicit tool limitations and future work
evidence_quotes.quote: Firstly, the S3D Tool needs to be improved and optimised.
a similar calculation sheet dedicated to the Command & Data Handling (C&DH) subsystem must also be created to standardize performance calculations and requirements tracking across all key systems.

notes_for_consistency: The paper is a system-level CubeSat design-method paper rather than an EPS-specific MBSE paper. EPS appears as one subsystem spreadsheet and multiple CUTE-DB power categories. Verification is discussed only at a general methodology level; no EPS-specific verification procedure is reported. SysML is not reported.
